arxiv-2305-17323.creator: Benjamin Grimmer, Danlin Li
arxiv-2305-17323.description: Abstract We consider (stochastic) subgradient methods for strongly convex but potentially nonsmooth non-Lipschitz optimization. arxiv-2408-07878.title: Passive Stability and Adaptive Control of Teleoperated System using Wave Variables and Predictor Techniques
arxiv-2408-07878.creator: Sridhar B Mudhangulla, Naveen K Rajarajan, Olugbenga Moses Anubi
arxiv-2408-07878.description:
A 2024 arXiv research paper by Sridhar B Mudhangulla, Naveen K Rajarajan, Olugbenga Moses Anubi. Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Florida State University
E-mail: nr21w@fsu.edu, sm19ch@fsu.edu, oanubi@fsu.edu

Abstract

This paper addresses the challenge of achieving stable adaptive teleoperation and improving the convergence rate in the presence of high communication time delays. We employ a passivity-based formalism to establish stability using wave variables and wave scattering techniques, and we enhance the convergence rate by combining it with predictor-based approaches.

arxiv-2409-15234.title: CA-MHFA: A Context-Aware Multi-Head Factorized Attentive Pooling for SSL-Based Speaker Verification
arxiv-2409-15234.creator: Junyi Peng, Ladislav Mošner, Lin Zhang, Oldřich Plchot, Themos Stafylakis, Lukáš Burget, Jan Černocký
arxiv-2409-15234.description: Abstract Self-supervised learning (SSL) models for speaker verification (SV) have gained significant attention in recent years. However, existing SSL-based SV systems often struggle to capture local temporal dependencies and generalize across different tasks. In this paper, we propose context-aware multi-head factorized attentive pooling (CA-MHFA), a lightweight framework that incorporates contextual information from surrounding frames.

arxiv-2411-03357.description: Abstract . Confidential computing on GPUs, like NVIDIA H100, mitigates the security risks of outsourced Large Language Models (LLMs) by implementing strong isolation and data encryption. Nonetheless, this encryption incurs a significant performance overhead, reaching up to 52.8% and 88.2% throughput drop when serving OPT-30B and OPT-66B, respectively. To address this challenge, we introduce PipeLLM , a user-transparent runtime system.
